text:
Dear Sir or Madam,

The Hagenbuch Cooperative has terminated the lease on my flat at Brunnenrain 71 in Uster. The notice came by registered post and I signed for it on 29 July 2026. It ends the lease at the end of January.

I want to rule one thing out straight away, because a friend asked me about it: this is not a case of them getting back at me for complaining. I have never asked the cooperative for repairs, never challenged my rent, never made any demands of that kind. There simply was no dispute of that sort.

What the notice is really about, I can't say for certain. The form itself gives no reason. When I rang Mr Ben Morgan, he said it was because I had not paid the heating and service charge bill of CHF 1835 by the deadline the cooperative had set in June. I don't accept that. I paid the full amount from my bank account the day before the deadline and have the confirmation. Mr Morgan insists the money only arrived after the deadline and that this is what counts. So we are stuck: he says it was late, I say it was on time, and I have no idea whether that is even the official reason for the notice or just something he said on the phone.

I'd like to know whether I can challenge this termination and what my chances are. I've lived here since 2022 and have always been a reliable tenant.

I'm attaching my lease so you can see the terms we agreed.

Yours faithfully,
Grace Wälti

Lease agreement for residential premises

Landlord: Hagenbuch Cooperative, Uster, represented by Ben Morgan
Tenant: Grace Wälti

Premises: 4-room flat, 2nd floor, Brunnenrain 71, 8610 Uster, with cellar compartment

Start: 1 August 2022
Duration: The lease is concluded for an indefinite period.

Notice: Either party may terminate the lease by giving three months' notice in writing, to the end of any month except December.

Monthly rent: CHF 3180, including advance payment for heating and service charges

Uster, 23 July 2022
Hagenbuch Cooperative, Ben Morgan
Grace Wälti
